title: PromptSign applies code-signing ideas to AI instructions
friendlyTitle: PromptSign checks who published an AI instruction file
summary: PromptSign signs AI skill folders and instruction files such as AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md, recording publisher identity and tamper-evident file fingerprints. Its command-line hooks can block unsigned or modified instructions, while verification can run offline.
friendlySummary: PromptSign adds a digital signature to AI skills and instruction files. It can tell you who signed the files and whether someone changed them later.
whyItMatters: As people install more third-party agent skills, provenance and integrity become part of software supply-chain hygiene. A valid signature does not prove instructions are safe, but it can show who published them and whether files changed after signing.
friendlyWhyItMatters: This can make shared agent tools easier to trust and audit. A signed file can still be harmful, so people must also review what it does.
